title: Senior Production Engineer  - DGX Cloud
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA DGX Cloud delivers AI services and endpoints for research and production workloads. We are looking for a Senior Production Engineer to build software and automation that make those services reliable, scalable, and safe to operate. The Production Engineering team works on large-scale distributed systems spanning internal and external model endpoints; regional control plane services that orchestrate workloads and route requests; and the GPU/CPU compute infrastructure where inference and agentic workloads run. Our work spans Kubernetes clusters across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, other partner cloud environments, and on-premises deployments.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Build and operate production software, automation, and tooling for control plane services, model deployments, and inference and agentic workloads across DGX Cloud environments.
  • Improve the reliability of inference and agentic platforms and services, including NVIDIA Cloud Functions, SGLang- and vLLM-based endpoints, and inference services built with NVIDIA Dynamo, through health validation, safer rollouts, observability, and recovery.
  • Improve endpoint availability, inference routing, capacity management, and service health to maintain predictable performance as workloads and demand change.
  • Use infrastructure as code and GitOps to deploy, configure, validate, upgrade, and recover services consistently across environments.
  • Build workflows for service enablement, model releases, handoff, deprecation, and ongoing operations; replace repeatable manual work with reliable automation.
  • Define and instrument SLIs and SLOs for inference and control plane services, including availability and latency, use error budgets to guide reliability improvements, and make production health visible to partner teams.
  • Participate in on-call and incident response, troubleshoot failures across routing, model runtimes, software, and infrastructure, and turn recurring issues into automation and durable fixes.
  • Collaborate with model, platform, storage, networking, security, and GPU infrastructure teams to design and operate services safely at scale.

What we need to see:

  • 8+ years of experience building or operating production services and large-scale distributed systems, including hands-on automation.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, Go, or a comparable language, with experience developing tools for production operations.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code, configuration management, or GitOps, and with building automation for repeatable service deployments and changes.
  • Strong knowledge of Linux, Kubernetes, containers, cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, and networking fundamentals; ability to diagnose failures in production.
  • Understanding of Production Engineering principles, including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, incident response, and reducing operational toil.
  • Experience instrumenting services and using metrics, logs, and traces to understand system behavior and improve reliability.
  • Clear technical communication and ability to work across engineering teams.
  • BS/MS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Familiarity with technologies such as vLLM, SGLang, PyTorch, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, CUDA, or NCCL, and with GPU performance analysis.
  • Experience building Kubernetes operators, controllers, workload orchestration services, fleet management systems, or self-healing automation.
  • Experience with Terraform, Argo CD, CI/CD, policy validation, or safe deployment and rollback systems.
  • Background with developing with AI tools and agents.
  • Experience with production AI inference or agentic workloads, including debugging issues across models, runtimes, Kubernetes, and hardware.

NVIDIA is leading the way in groundbreaking developments in Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing and Visualization. The GPU, our invention, serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and is at the heart of our products and services. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hard-working people on the planet working for us. If you're creative, hard-working and self-motivated, we want to hear from you!

We are now packing tens of billions of transistors in a chip to meet the growing computing demand. We are looking for a top ASIC Design Engineer to join our team. In this role, you should have real passion for RTL design implementation and methodologies that enable high quality system-level IP design.


What you'll be doing:

  • Be an integral part of the team defining and developing system-level RTL and methodologies to measure performance on the industry's leading GPUs/SOCs.
  • Design and implement RTL features - work through the entire design cycle for SOC.
  • Run and debug RTL checks to ensure design quality (e.g. CDC, RDC, Lint, Synthesis, Logic-Equivalence and more)
  • Define, develop, and automate flows and methodologies to efficiently build and support a system-level IP
  • Work with architects, designers, verification and SW engineers to accomplish your tasks.

What we need to see:

  • B.Tech or M.Tech in Electronics or Computer Engineering.
  • 3+ years of relevant industry experience.
  • Experienced in RTL design (Verilog), System-On-Chip design/implementation flows, and design automation.
  • Good understanding of SOC/IP (u)architecture (e.g., data flow, control, multiple clock/power domains handling, latency analysis).
  • Strong coding skills in Perl, Python or other industry-standard scripting languages.
  • Excellent debugging and analytical skills.
  • Exposure to design and verification tools (dc_shell or equivalent synthesis tools, VCS or equivalent simulation tools, debug tools like Debussy, GDB).
  • Great communication and collaboration skills to interact within the team and with cross functional teams.
  • Adept at using AI tools to enhance productivity and solve complicated problems

NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We employ some of the most forward-thinking and innovative people in the world. Are you passionate about joining our life’s work to amplify human imagination and intelligence? If you are creative, collaborative, and have real passion for design, methodology, and automation, we want to hear from you!

title: Senior DevOps Engineer - Robotics Simulation
descriptionHtml:

Leveraging the power of NVIDIA's AI and GPU technologies, Isaac Sim offers a realistic and scalable environment for training, validating, and optimizing robots for real-world scenarios.


You will work closely with Isaac Sim developers, QA, and infrastructure teams to make software delivery faster, more reliable, and reproducible. Your work will enable engineers to identify regressions early and deliver high-quality releases across supported platforms.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Design, develop, and operate CI/CD pipelines for building, testing, packaging, and releasing Isaac Sim and its components.
  • Own GPU-enabled CI runners and test environments across on-premises and cloud infrastructure, including provisioning, scheduling, capacity planning, and recovery.
  • Partner with developers and QA to integrate automated simulation, integration, and performance tests into pull-request validation, nightly builds, and release qualification.
  • Improve build and test turnaround through parallel execution, caching, efficient GPU utilization, and systematic analysis of bottlenecks.
  • Develop reproducible environments and versioned artifacts, managing dependencies, containers, and compatibility across supported operating systems and GPU software configurations.
  • Build dashboards, logging, and alerts that expose pipeline health, infrastructure availability, test failures, and performance trends.
  • Diagnose failures across build tools, operating systems, containers, GPU drivers, networking, and simulation runtimes; improve failure reporting and reduce flaky tests.
  • Strengthen release automation through artifact traceability, quality gates, dependency scanning, and secure credential management.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field (equivalent experience).
  • 5+ years of relevant experience in DevOps, infrastructure engineering, build and release engineering, or software engineering, with ownership of CI/CD systems.
  • Strong Python and Bash programming skills and experience developing maintainable automation.
  • Hands-on experience with Git-based development and CI/CD platforms such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or Jenkins.
  • Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills, including networking, storage, processes, and performance.
  • Experience with Docker, container orchestration, and infrastructure automation using tools such as Kubernetes, Terraform, or Ansible.
  • Experience supporting automated tests, managing build artifacts and dependencies, and troubleshooting complex software pipelines.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate across engineering teams and drive infrastructure improvements.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Omniverse, OpenUSD, or other robotics simulation platforms.
  • Experience operating GPU infrastructure and debugging NVIDIA driver, CUDA, or graphics-runtime issues.
  • Familiarity with C++ build systems, CMake, Python packaging, and software distribution across Linux and Windows.
  • A track record of improving CI reliability, reducing build times, and increasing infrastructure utilization.
  • Experience securing CI for open-source projects and untrusted contributions.

title: Director, Software Engineering – Cloud Compute and Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking an engineering director to lead the software teams behind our bare-metal datacenters and cloud compute infrastructure. The organization supports hundreds of megawatts of datacenter capacity already online, with more capacity coming. You will build the software that makes this growing physical infrastructure available as reliable, secure, and efficient compute services for NVIDIA engineering.


Our team provides NVIDIA’s continuous integration (CI) infrastructure: the environment where hardware, firmware, drivers, networking, and system software are integrated and tested on their path to production. You will enable engineering teams to bring up preproduction systems, reproduce failures, validate changes, and move platforms toward production readiness. The fleet spans multiple hardware generations and maturity levels: x86 and Arm servers, GPUs, DPUs, high-speed networking, storage, and rack-scale, liquid-cooled systems. Platforms such as Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin illustrate the breadth of compute and interconnect technology involved. This role combines hands-on systems judgment with leadership of the teams making that diversity manageable at scale.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead software engineering teams responsible for cloud compute, bare-metal fleet management, and CI infrastructure, owning architecture, implementation, deployment, and operations.
  • Set the technical direction for compute control planes, resource provisioning, topology-aware placement, reservations, and capacity management across physical servers, virtual machines, and containers.
  • Automate the bare-metal lifecycle: hardware discovery and inventory, server bring-up, imaging, firmware and driver configuration, out-of-band management, health checks, reprovisioning, and recovery.
  • Build CI services that allocate the right hardware, provision repeatable test environments, record hardware and software configurations, collect diagnostics, and restore systems to a known state. Shorten the path from a hardware or software change to actionable validation results.
  • Keep engineering services dependable while supporting evolving preproduction hardware and software. Define service-level objectives, isolate failures, improve observability, and turn incidents and recurring test-infrastructure failures into engineering fixes.
  • Measure and improve hardware onboarding time, provisioning speed, CI queue time, productive fleet utilization, recovery time, and cost efficiency as capacity expands.
  • Set engineering standards for design and code reviews, automated testing, secure development, release quality, and safe changes to production systems.
  • Hire, coach, and retain engineers and engineering managers. Establish clear ownership, develop technical leaders, and build teams that deliver consistently over multiple release cycles.
  • Partner with hardware, firmware, drivers, networking, storage, security, and validation teams to onboard platforms and diagnose failures across system boundaries. Translate engineering users’ needs into clear priorities and technical decisions.
  • Work with datacenter operations and facilities teams to bring additional capacity online. Connect rack power, cooling, physical topology, and hardware-health telemetry to provisioning, placement, serviceability, and operational readiness.

What we need to see:

  • 15+ overall years of experience in software engineering, distributed systems, or cloud infrastructure, including 7+ years leading engineering teams and experience managing engineering managers.
  • Direct engineering ownership of the underlying services of a public or private compute cloud, such as AWS EC2, Google Compute Engine, Azure Compute, OCI Compute, or a comparable infrastructure-as-a-service platform.
  • Strong technical depth in distributed systems, Linux, virtualization, containers, and the networking and storage services that support large compute fleets.
  • Experience building software and automation for bare-metal infrastructure, including server provisioning, hardware inventory, firmware or operating-system lifecycle management, and recovery across heterogeneous systems.
  • Experience running production infrastructure with demanding availability requirements, including failure isolation, incident response, observability, and reliable deployment and recovery mechanisms.
  • The ability to guide architecture, evaluate implementation choices, and debug complex interactions among hardware, firmware, drivers, operating systems, and distributed services with senior engineers.
  • A record of sustained ownership as platforms evolve, with measurable improvements in reliability, scalability, or engineering delivery. Strong communication, collaboration, and people-development skills.
  • A degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience building or operating OpenStack infrastructure, particularly Nova, Neutron, Cinder, or Ironic, or contributing to related open-source projects.
  • Engineering leadership spanning compute control planes and site reliability, including multi-tenant isolation, scheduling, placement, and capacity allocation.
  • Experience with GPU clusters, rack-scale computing, NVLink, InfiniBand or high-speed Ethernet, and AI or high-performance computing workloads.
  • Experience supporting preproduction hardware, new product introduction, or hardware-in-the-loop CI, including repeatable validation environments and systematic regression isolation.
  • Familiarity with liquid-cooled, high-density datacenters and how power, thermal constraints, cooling, and component health affect fleet availability and scheduling and delivery of compute platforms across multiple regions, datacenters, or hybrid-cloud environments, including fleet upgrades and workload migration with minimal service disruption.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Prediction - Autonomous Driving
descriptionHtml:
Intelligent machines powered by Artificial Intelligence computers that can learn, reason and interact with people are no longer science fiction. GPU Deep Learning has provided the foundation for machines to learn, perceive, reason and solve problems. Now, NVIDIA’s GPU runs Deep Learning algorithms, simulating human intelligence, and acts as the brain of computers, robots and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world.


We are now looking for an extraordinary Senior Engineer to develop and productize NVIDIA’s autonomous driving solutions. Efforts will include data collection prioritization and planning, labeling prioritization, labeling efficiency optimization, so that value of data is maximized

title: Production Application Engineer, Enterprise
descriptionHtml:

  • 5+ years of experience in hardware system engineering, production engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related role.
  • Strong understanding of server manufacturing processes, including module assembly (L6), system integration (L10), rack integration (L11), test, and quality control.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills — able to represent NVIDIA in cross-functional and cross-company technical discussions.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer - Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Senior Site Reliability Engineer – Infrastructure to help build, operate, and improve the reliability, performance, and scalability of infrastructure platforms supporting critical engineering environments across Taiwan and APAC. You will combine strong infrastructure expertise with automation and SRE practices to deploy, troubleshoot, and operate highly reliable infrastructure across compute, storage, virtualization, and container platforms.

title: SRAM Circuit Design Engineer - New College Grad 2026
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been redefining computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. Today, we're tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing — an era in which our GPUs act as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. Come join our diverse team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.


The Digital IP (DIP) group at NVIDIA develops IP for every chip designed at NVIDIA. This group works closely with internal SOC design, silicon testing, and productization teams that turn our IP into products that change the world. One of the roles fulfilled by the DIP group is to develop sophisticated SRAM compilers that are used extensively by our SOC design partners. We are looking to hire a skilled and creative SRAM circuit designer to help achieve these goals in a high-visibility position.


What you'll be doing:

  • Embedded SRAM design: Transistor-level circuit design, supervising layout implementation, physical and logical verification, and debug of SRAM macros.
  • SRAM compiler development: Envisioning, defining, and coding more efficient ways to automate the simultaneous assembly and validation of multiple unique SRAM macros using NVIDIA's extensive compute resources.
  • Advanced development: Exploring the potential of future process nodes and developing techniques to achieve optimal power, performance, and area characteristics.
  • Guiding SOC design, silicon test, and productization efforts: Collaborate with SOC design partners to help them achieve their overall performance and cost goals, guide the silicon test and characterization efforts, and working with productization teams to prepare new silicon for the demanding requirements of real-world applications.

What we need to see:

  • Master's degree or higher in Electrical Engineer or other related field (or equivalent experience).
  • SRAM design experience with a strong background in digital circuit design, layout, and validation on advanced FinFET and nanosheet processes.
  • Design experience in single-port, dual-port, or register file SRAM-based macros required, including complex circuits such as self-timed logic and sense-amplifiers.
  • Familiarity with Cadence Virtuoso schematic and layout capture tools
  • Shown dewlivery of silicon IP into production.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Shown written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Skills in AI coding and analysis tools such as Codex and Claude Code.
  • Silicon testing/debug experience.

title: Senior STA Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is seeking a Physical Design and Timing Engineer to join our silicon implementation team. This role focuses on timing analysis, timing closure, and signoff quality across complex ASIC and SoC designs. You will work closely with physical design, front-end design, methodology, and CAD teams to drive robust implementation at advanced process nodes. This is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys deep analysis, problem solving, and improving quality at block and full-chip levels.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Drive static timing analysis and timing closure for block and/or full-chip designs.
  • Develop, review, and debug timing constraints, scenarios, and signoff checks.
  • Analyze setup, hold, noise, and variation-related timing issues and drive closure with cross-functional teams.
  • Partner with physical design engineers on floorplan, CTS, route, ECO, and convergence activities.
  • Review reports, identify root causes of violations, and recommend high-quality fixes with minimal design impact.
  • Improve timing methodology, automation, and debug efficiency using Tcl, Perl, and/or Python.

What we need to see:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of experience in ASIC or SoC physical design, timing analysis, or implementation.
  • Strong understanding of static timing analysis fundamentals, timing constraints, and timing closure.
  • Hands-on experience with industry-standard EDA tools such as PrimeTime, ICC2, Innovus, Tempus, or equivalent.
  • Experience debugging setup/hold violations, clocking issues, and ECO impacts.
  • Solid scripting skills in Tcl plus familiarity with Perl or Python.
  • Good communication skills and ability to work across design, CAD, and verification teams.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with advanced-node implementation and signoff.
  • Knowledge of MMMC flows, SI, OCV/AOCV/POCV, and power-aware timing analysis.
  • Experience improving timing methodology or developing reusable automation.

title: Cloud Services Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Joining NVIDIA's DGX Cloud Team means contributing to the infrastructure that powers our innovative AI research. This team focuses on optimizing efficiency and resiliency of ML workloads, as well as developing scalable AI infrastructure tools and services. Our objective is to deliver a stable, scalable environment for AI researchers, providing them with the vital resources and scale to champion innovation.

We are seeking a distributed software engineer to join our team! As a Senior engineer, you'll be instrumental in developing and optimizing AI infrastructure services to bring peak AI performance and high resiliency for DGX Cloud. Your expertise in cloud services software architecture that drives the full resilience stack that will deliver an AI platform that redefines what is possible. This is an exceptional opportunity to push the boundaries of technology and shape the future of AI and the Cloud, and work with a world-class team of like-minded engineers.

What You Will Be Doing:

As a software engineer specializing in backend development, you'll work in a dedicated team to enhance the infrastructure and products that underpin NVIDIA's AI platforms. Your work will be essential in enabling innovative AI research, focusing on:

  • Developing solutions at the intersection of machine learning, distributed systems, and high-performance computing, supplying to the advancement of AI technologies.

  • Designing, developing, and optimizing (micro-)services orchestrated by Kubernetes to provide large-scale AI training workflows on AI training supercomputers located at major CSPs, with resiliency and efficiency.

  • Co-designing and implementing the APIs that allow these services to integrate vertically with NVIDIA's resiliency stacks, ranging from tier-0 telemetry services to break/fix automation services to checkpoint and execution systems.

  • Crafting a submission abstraction that enables model engineers and training platforms/frameworks to seamlessly submit long-running training jobs while hiding the complexity of handling infrastructure failures, running job lifecycles with auto-restarts on failure, ensuring full efficiency, and promptly advising users.

  • Crafting these services to be modular, enabling them to be coordinated with and deployed onto on-premises AI clusters that apply NVIDIA Hardware and Cloud services.

What We Need To See:

  • A Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science or a related technical field (or equivalent experience).

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in backend development, preferably with Python, Go, C/C++, or similar high-performance languages.

  • Consistent track record of building and scaling large-scale distributed systems.

  • Experience with cloud computing platforms such as AWS, Azure, and GCP, as well as container technologies like Docker and Kubernetes, and HPC/AI platforms such as Slurm.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Real world experience in DL frameworks, orchestrators like PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, and Ray

  • Experience in developing a framework plugin architecture that allows the framework to be integrated with the cluster scheduler visibly to the users

  • Strong understanding of NVIDIA GPUs, network technologies, and their failure patterns.

  • Experience with AI models and AI based tools.

  • Provide references to your code contributions.

NVIDIA leads the way in groundbreaking developments in Artificial Intelligence, High-Performance Computing, and Visualization. The GPU, our invention, serves as the visual cortex of modern computers and is at the heart of our products and services. Our work opens up new universes to explore, enables amazing creativity and discovery, and powers what were once science fiction inventions, from artificial intelligence to autonomous cars. NVIDIA is looking for exceptional people like you to help us accelerate the next wave of artificial intelligence!

title: Senior Research Scientist, AI for Cybersecurity
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Senior Scientist to lead research on advancing AI models and agents for cybersecurity and applying them to important security problems. This includes improving capabilities such as security reasoning, code and system understanding, planning, tool use, long-horizon investigation, and effective collaboration with human defenders, as well as applying these capabilities to vulnerability discovery, secure development, threat and anomaly detection, malware and attack analysis, incident investigation, security validation, and automated defense.


The ideal candidate will advance the underlying models, agent architectures, data, training and post-training methods, and evaluations needed for effective cybersecurity, while addressing the requirements of real security environments: high precision, robustness to adaptive adversaries, explainability, privacy, secure deployment, and effective human oversight. You will connect foundational AI and security research with practical tools and workflows that materially improve prevention, detection, investigation, and response. NVIDIA is a leader in accelerated computing and AI systems. This role offers the opportunity to set research direction, influence future platforms, and translate foundational advances into practical capabilities in collaboration with research, product, and engineering teams.


What you'll be doing:

  • Define a high-impact research agenda and lead projects that advance AI models and agents for cybersecurity and apply them to important security problems.
  • Improve model and agent capabilities for security reasoning, code and system understanding, planning, tool use, memory, long-horizon investigation, and collaboration with human defenders through advances in architectures, data, training, post-training, and evaluation.
  • Develop AI-powered capabilities for vulnerability discovery, secure development, threat detection, malware analysis, incident investigation, security validation, and automated defense that are robust to adversarial manipulation, uncertainty, distribution shift, and incomplete or noisy operational data.
  • Build and evaluate prototypes in realistic environments, measuring detection quality, false positives, time to insight, analyst effectiveness, security risk, and operational scalability.
  • Collaborate across AI, security, research, engineering, and product teams; publish original research; mentor researchers and interns; and help translate advances into deployed capabilities.

What we need to see:

  • A Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years of relevant experience. An established record of research excellence demonstrated through influential publications, open-source systems, patents, technology transfer, or substantial research collaborations.
  • Deep expertise in one or more relevant areas such as agentic AI, model training, reasoning and tool use, machine learning for security, vulnerability research, program analysis, software security, intrusion detection, malware analysis, or security operations.
  • Experience defining and leading ambiguous, multi-disciplinary research projects and providing technical mentorship.
  • Strong experimental and prototyping skills; Python and relevant AI/ML frameworks, including experience training, adapting, or evaluating models or agents; experience with systems software, security tooling, or large-scale data systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both AI researchers and security practitioners.

Are you a creative, collaborative, and self-directed researcher who can advance AI agents for cybersecurity, expand what they can do for defenders, and turn new ideas into high-impact research and technology? If so, we want to hear from you!

descriptionHtml:

  • Exposure to ASIC design and verification tools (VCS or equivalent, Verdi, GDB).

title: Senior Manager, Graphics Systems Software and Compute Graphics Chips
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics and accelerated computing for more than 30 years. We are now reinventing graphics with AI. Advances in graphics system software, compute graphics, and neural rendering are expanding what GPUs can deliver across visual computing, robotics, and automotive platforms.


We are seeking a deeply technical Senior Engineering Manager to lead our graphics software organization in Finland. You will lead an experienced team delivering graphics system software for automotive and robotics while growing its contributions to NVIDIA’s overall graphics direction. Your scope spans GPU and SoC bring-up, graphics API development, and platform integration, with opportunities to contribute to technologies such as neural shading and Slang. Working with architects and partner teams across NVIDIA, you will define a clear technical strategy and roadmap, and establish the team’s capabilities to deliver the next generation of graphics software. This role combines technical leadership, team development, and execution. You will partner with senior architects and engineering leaders to set focused roadmaps, deliver production-quality software, and develop the skills needed for new graphics opportunities. You will also advance how the team builds software by applying AI-assisted development and agentic automation.


What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Lead and develop a team delivering graphics system software and advancing compute graphics.
  • Own team strategy, roadmaps, priorities, quality, and delivery commitments.
  • Drive execution across GPU and SoC enablement, Vulkan and OpenGL drivers, CUDA-based graphics, platform integration, and production releases.
  • Collaborate with GPU architecture, hardware, research, and platform teams on technical direction and hardware/software co-design.
  • Expand the team’s contributions to NVIDIA’s broader graphics strategy.
  • Mentor engineers and technical leaders while hiring and developing outstanding talent.
  • Improve development, validation, and support through better engineering practices, infrastructure, and AI-assisted and agentic workflows.

What We Need to See:

title: Senior Solutions Architect, AI and HPC Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:

At NVIDIA, our solutions architects work across product, engineering, sales, developer relations, business development, and partner teams to help customers design, deploy, and optimize AI infrastructure for the energy industry. What we need to see:

title: Senior Software Engineer — Active Safety for Autonomous Vehicles
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is driving the autonomous vehicle revolution, delivering AI-powered visual computing platforms that define tomorrow’s mobility. As vehicles become supercomputers on wheels, our challenge is to build the software foundation that makes advanced driver assistance and safety features truly intelligent.


We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer based in Stuttgart, Germany, to work directly with automotive customers on the integration and productionization of active safety software for the NVIDIA DRIVE platform. Your primary focus will be adapting NVIDIA software to vehicle platforms, diagnosing system-level issues and validating active safety functions and intervention logic (e.g., AEB. AES. ,,,) behavior in development and production vehicles. You will work across perception, fusion, planning, and vehicle integration to trace problems through the full software chain, identify root causes, implement or coordinate appropriate solutions, and turn findings into actionable input for NVIDIA engineering teams.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Integrate and adapt NVIDIA DRIVE Active Safety software on customer development and production vehicles.
  • Triage and analyze issues across the active safety chain, from sensor input through perception and fusion to maneuver behavior.
  • Collaborate with customer teams and NVIDIA engineering teams across Europe, the US, APAC, and India to identify root causes, deliver program-level solutions, and drive longer-term product corrections.
  • Configure and tune active safety software for different vehicle platforms, sensor configurations, vehicle geometries and braking performance.
  • Implement targeted C++ or Python adaptations, debugging tools, and analysis workflows where needed to resolve customer integration and functional issues.
  • Measure functional performance through recorded-data replay and in-vehicle testing, and communicate findings clearly to customers and NVIDIA engineering teams.
  • Work on vehicle bring-up, software flashing, data logging, testing and functional validation.

What we need to see:

  • Strong background in ADAS development and triage, with at least 8+ years of experience including in-vehicle activities.
  • Solid understanding of Active Safety functions from concept to validation, including hazard mitigation and functional safety principles.
  • Proven experience designing and implementing threat assessment algorithms, including time-to-collision (TTC). Hands-on development of longitudinal and lateral intervention planners — translating threat assessments into smooth, physically feasible braking and steering commands.
  • Strong understanding of radar and camera perception outputs — including object confidence, classification uncertainty.
  • Proficiency in Linux and/or QNX-based embedded environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to systematically isolate issues using log analysis, data review, and cross-functional technical coordination.
  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical, or Automotive Engineering (or equivalent practical experience).
  • Excellent communication skills — able to explain technical findings clearly and concisely across engineering teams.
  • Valid driver’s license and readiness for road testing and travel.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with active safety software, or closely related perception, fusion or planning and controller work. Production experience with camera- and radar-based active safety systems.
  • Experience integrating ADAS software into customer vehicle platforms and supporting automotive series programs. Experience with commercial vehicles (heavy vans, trucks, or buses) and familiarity with commercial-vehicle-specific active safety regulations.
  • Deep understanding of Euro NCAP protocols, including scoring optimization for "Safe Driving" and "Crash Avoidance" stages (e.g., VRU protection, junction scenarios, and DSM requirements). 
  • Experience with data-driven development loops, including fleet-data triage, corner-case analysis and feedback to model-training teams.
  • Hands-on experience with AI/ML workflows and deep neural network development or integration — e.g., in perception tasks such as object detection, segmentation, or depth estimation

title: Math Libraries Intern, cuEST - Summer 2027
descriptionHtml:

NVIDIA is looking for software engineering interns to join the math libraries team building cuEST, a CUDA-X math library that accelerates quantum chemistry on NVIDIA GPUs. Launched in March 2026, cuEST provides accelerated APIs for essential functions in electronic structure computations, starting with Gaussian-basis quantum chemistry. These capabilities power applications ranging from drug discovery to semiconductor process development. We are constantly working to improve the feature set, performance, and technology stack of cuEST. If the idea of helping expand the frontiers of electronic structure theory excites you, come join our team and help us build GPU-accelerated software used by quantum chemists around the world.


During your internship, you will work with senior engineers on the cuEST team who will mentor you and guide you in developing highly optimized algorithms and numerical methods for quantum chemistry. Projects may involve implementing new quantum chemistry primitives, defining APIs, analyzing and improving GPU performance, finding solutions for difficult numerical corner cases, and other software engineering work that goes into shipping a production CUDA-X library.


What you’ll be doing:

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

title: Architecture Energy Modeling Engineer
descriptionHtml:
At NVIDIA, we pride ourselves in having energy efficient products. We believe that continuing to maintain our products' energy efficiency compared to the competition is key to our continued success. Our team is responsible for researching, developing, and deploying methodologies to help NVIDIA's products become more energy efficient; and is responsible for building energy models that integrate into architectural simulators, RTL simulation, and emulation platforms. Key responsibilities include developing techniques to model, analyze, and reduce the power consumption of NVIDIA GPUs.

As a member of the Power Modeling, Methodology, and Analysis Team, you will collaborate with Architects, Performance Engineers, Software Engineers, ASIC Design Engineers, and Physical Design teams to study and implement energy modeling techniques for NVIDIA's next-generation GPUs and Tegra SOCs. Your contributions will help us gain early insight into the energy consumption of graphics and artificial intelligence workloads, and will allow us to influence architectural, design, and power management improvements.

  • Correlate the predicted energy from models created at different stages of the design cycle, with the goal of bridging early estimates to silicon.
  • Develop tools to debug energy inefficiencies observed in various workloads run on silicon, RTL and architectural simulators. Work with architects to fix the identified energy inefficiencies.
  • Work with performance, verification and emulation methodology and infrastructure development teams to integrate energy models into their platforms.
  • Prototype new architectural features, create an energy model, and analyze the system impact.

What we need to see:

  • MS degree with 3+ year experience in related fields or equivalent experience
  • Strong coding skills, preferably in Python, C++.
  • Background in machine learning, AI, and/or statistical modeling.
  • Interest in computer architecture and energy-efficient GPU designs.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Bare Metal Infrastructure – DGX Cloud
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA DGX Cloud builds large-scale GPU infrastructure that powers the world’s most demanding AI workloads. Our Bare Metal Infrastructure team owns the software that turns newly racked hardware into reliable, validated production capacity. We’re looking for a software engineer with deep systems engineering instincts — someone who writes production code and understands how servers, firmware, BMCs, and networks actually behave. You’ll work across the full bare-metal lifecycle: new platform introduction, firmware qualification, automated provisioning, validation, remediation, and handoff to production. We use AI agents and LLM tools heavily in how we build software, and we want someone excited to push that further.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Designing, building, and maintaining production services for bare-metal discovery, provisioning, hardware validation, firmware upgrades, auditing, and repair across large GPU fleets.
  • Developing integrations with Redfish and vendor BMC interfaces to manage server state, collect inventory and health data, enforce configuration, and drive recovery — handling vendor differences in code.
  • Contributing to and reviewing code in our Rust codebase, and building supporting tools and services in Go and Python.
  • Turning recurring hardware, firmware, and connectivity failures into automated detection, validation, and repair workflows.
  • Defining and implementing automated validation and handoff criteria for new platforms, firmware releases, and rack-scale deployments.
  • Debugging complex failures across hardware, firmware, Linux, networking, and provisioning services, and feeding what you learn back into the software.
  • Partnering with server and component vendors and with internal platform, networking, datacenter, and production engineering teams to resolve cross-boundary issues.
  • Using AI agents and LLM tools daily to write, review, and test code and to investigate failures, and helping shape how the team builds with AI.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years building production infrastructure software, automation, or services, including substantial hands-on work with bare-metal server systems.
  • Strong programming skills in Rust, Go, or Python, with a track record of designing, testing, shipping, and maintaining production code and willingness to work in Rust regularly.
  • Deep knowledge of enterprise server hardware from multiple vendors (Dell, Supermicro, Lenovo, HPE), including BMCs, BIOS/UEFI, and firmware management.
  • Direct experience with Redfish and IPMI for provisioning, health inspection, power management, or fault diagnosis, and with network boot (PXE/iPXE, DHCP, HTTP boot).
  • Strong Linux knowledge: boot process, kernel and driver interactions, hardware discovery, and low-level failure analysis.
  • Solid datacenter networking fundamentals with the ability to trace connectivity problems across host, management, and infrastructure networks.
  • Demonstrated, regular use of AI agents and LLM tools in software development, with strong interest in improving and the judgment to validate what they produce.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Production experience writing Rust.
  • Experience with NVIDIA DGX or NVL72 systems, NVLink, InfiniBand, Spectrum-X, or BlueField DPUs.
  • Background in hardware qualification, rack-scale bring-up, firmware certification, or new product introduction, including safe, scalable workflows for fleet firmware upgrades, configuration enforcement, hardware replacement, and recovery.
  • Experience with Kubernetes, GitOps/Argo CD, or fleet-management platforms.
  • Examples of AI-driven tooling or workflows you’ve built that measurably changed how you or your team ships software.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
152,000 USD – 241,500 USD for Level 3; and 184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 3, 2026.

title: Senior Package Layout Engineer - Hardware
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself. Our invention of the GPU sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. Today, research in artificial intelligence is booming worldwide, which calls for highly scalable and massively parallel computation horsepower that NVIDIA GPUs excel. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can address, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work , to amplify human creativity and intelligence. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join our diverse team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world!


NVIDIA's GPUs and SOCs are the world leaders in power, performance and efficiency. We are continually innovating to deliver new and creative, unusual solutions to extraordinary problems in a wide range of sectors. To this purpose, we are now seeking a hard-working Senior Package Layout Engineer who is committed to making a difference in the world through their contributions! This position will collaborate with Technical Package Lead and different design teams in the design and development of sophisticated, detailed layout of IC substrates for NVIDIA products. In addition, work with design teams to plan schedules, resolve costs, manufacturing, and electrical design issues.


What you'll be doing:

  • As part of a Layout team, you will collaborate to implement high speed/density ASIC packages.
  • Perform substrate breakout patterns for ASIC packages.
  • Optimize package pinout incorporating system level trade-offs of pins assignment.
  • Help perform package routing, placement, stack-up, reference plane and power distribution using Cadence APD or SiP tool suite.
  • Propose layout design trade-offs to the Technical Package Lead for resolution and implementation.
  • Conduct design feasibility studies to evaluate the Package design goals for size, cost, and system performance.
  • Develop symbols and CAD library databases using Cadence APD design tools
  • Develop methodologies to improve layout productivity


What we need to see:

  • Hold a B.S. Electrical Engineering or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years experience in PCB Layout of graphics cards, motherboards, line cards or other related technology. Experience with HDI designs is a plus
  • Proven experience in substrate layout of wire bond and flip chip packages, preferred
  • Significant background with Cadence APD or SiP and/or PCB layout tools (including Constraint Manager)
  • Solid understanding of high-speed design signal integrity practices
  • Experience with Virtuoso and Calibre is a plus
  • Experience using Valor is helpful

title: Senior Physical AI Data Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is building the next generation of AI and advanced data technologies for Physical AI. Our MLOps Ground Truth (GT) team develops large-scale data infrastructure, tooling, AI-based GT generation systems, DNN auto labeling, VLM labeling, and agentic workflows for global automotive and robotics partners.

We are looking for a Senior Physical AI Data Engineer to architect, build, and scale this global data ecosystem. In this role, you will drive the development of large scale automated labeling systems, and LLM- and agent-powered workflows that transform multimodal sensor data into high-quality datasets for model training and validation. You will collaborate closely with human operations and research teams to deliver reliable, scalable and ultra high quality GT data for autonomous driving and robotics.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Develop and productionize AI-powered auto-labeling workflows using computer vision models, vision-language models, and AI agents, integrating human review where needed.
  • Design and implement MLOps capabilities for reproducible training and inference, model and dataset versioning, evaluation, deployment, and lifecycle management.
  • Build observability and data quality frameworks covering pipeline health, job execution, labeling quality, data lineage, and GT release readiness.
  • Optimize distributed processing and GPU inference workloads to improve throughput, resource utilization, cost efficiency, and release turnaround time.
  • Drive technical decisions and cross-functional execution with perception, autolabeling modeling, data operations, and partner-facing teams to translate requirements into production solutions.
  • Establish engineering best practices while leading complex technical initiatives.

What We Need to See

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of relevant industry experience building production data infrastructure, MLOps platforms, or large-scale machine learning systems.
  • Strong programming skills in Python and C++, with experience designing maintainable, well-tested software and troubleshooting complex production systems.
  • A solid understanding of computer vision, machine learning, VLMs, and AI agent development, including evaluation and production integration.
  • Experience building reliable data pipelines with data validation, versioning, lineage, and monitoring.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex projects, make sound architectural decisions, and deliver measurable improvements in scalability, reliability, or performance.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across global, multidisciplinary teams.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd

  • Experience with Physical AI, autonomous driving, or robotics data platforms, particularly multimodal sensor processing and GT generation.
  • Hands-on experience developing and evaluating AI agents for auto-labeling, quality assurance, or workflow automation.
  • Experience with vision-language models, multimodal foundation models, or model-assisted annotation workflows.
  • Experience delivering multi-region data platforms with access controls, data governance, and regional data-handling requirements.
  • Fluent English communication and writing skills.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward‑thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you’re passionate about AI, data, defining what the model can and cannot learn, and enabling world‑class AI models with high‑quality data, we want to hear from you!

title: GenAI Algorithms Intern – Model Optimization for Inference
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is at the forefront of the generative AI revolution! The Algorithmic Model Optimization Team focuses on optimizing generative AI models such as large language models (LLMs), vision-language models (VLMs), and diffusion models for maximal inference efficiency using techniques ranging from quantization, speculative decoding, sparsity, distillation, pruning to neural architecture search, and automated deployment strategies.

Our work includes conducting applied research to improve model efficiency as well as developing an innovative open-source model optimization platform (NVIDIA Model Optimizer). Our software is used both internally across NVIDIA and externally by research and engineering teams alike developing best-in-class AI models.

We are seeking a GenAI Algorithms Intern to help optimize state-of-the-art generative AI models like LLMs, VLMs, multimodal and diffusion models. In this role, you will design, implement, and productionize model optimization algorithms for inference and deployment on NVIDIA’s latest hardware platforms. The focus is on ease of use, compute and memory efficiency, and achieving the best accuracy–performance tradeoffs through software–hardware co-design.

Your work will span multiple layers of the AI software stack—ranging from algorithm design to integration—within NVIDIA’s ecosystem (Model Optimizer, NeMo/Megatron, TensorRT-LLM) and open-source frameworks (PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, SGLang). You may also dive deeper into GPU-level optimization, including custom kernel development with CUDA and Triton.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Help design and build modular, scalable model optimization software platforms that deliver exceptional user experiences while supporting diverse AI models and optimization techniques.
  • Explore, develop, and integrate innovative deep learning optimization algorithms (quantization, speculative decoding, sparsity, distillation, pruning, neural architecture search) into NVIDIA's AI software stack.
  • Deploy optimized models into leading open-source inference frameworks and contribute specialized APIs, model-level optimizations, and new features tailored to the latest NVIDIA hardware capabilities.
  • Collaborate with NVIDIA teams on model optimization solutions for customer use cases, aiming for optimal end-to-end workflows and balanced accuracy–performance trade-offs.
  • Conduct GPU kernel-level profiling to identify and capitalize on hardware and software optimization opportunities (e.g., efficient attention kernels, KV cache optimization, parallelism strategies).

What we need to see:

  • Pursuing a Master's or PhD in Computer Science, AI, Applied Math, or a related field.
  • Strong deep learning background and hands-on experience with language models.
  • Solid foundation in algorithms and programming.
  • Proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and modern ML frameworks/tools.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with model optimization and efficiency (e.g., quantization, distillation, pruning).
  • Contributions to PyTorch, JAX, vLLM, SGLang, or other machine learning training and inference frameworks.
  • Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning generative AI models on large-scale GPU clusters.
  • Knowledge of GPU architectures and compilation stacks, and the ability to analyze and debug end-to-end performance.
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA’s deep learning SDKs (Model Optimizer, NeMo).

Increasingly known as “the AI computing company” and widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. Are you creative, motivated, and love a challenge? If so, we want to hear from you! Come, join our model optimization group, where you can help build real-time, cost-effective computing platforms driving our success in this exciting and rapidly-growing field.

descriptionHtml:

title: Senior Executive Assistant
descriptionHtml:

The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, with a mission to enable leaders and teams to perform at their best. You bring initiative, critical thinking, and a collaborative spirit to everything you do, and you’re motivated by the knowledge that your operational excellence helps drive innovation that truly matters.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Partner closely with the CSO, staying aligned with evolving priorities and anticipating needs; apply sound judgment on what needs the CSO’s attention, what to resolve independently, and when to interrupt, making decisions within agreed boundaries, redirecting requests, and pushing back diplomatically.
  • Manage calendars across global time zones, evaluating competing requests and protecting time for preparation and focused work.
  • Prepare the CSO for internal, customer, and partner meetings with clear objectives, relevant pre-reads, and clarity on decisions needed; for selected meetings, capture decisions, owners, and deadlines, and follow through on commitments.
  • Contribute to the planning of and independently execute key meetings, events, and off-sites, and maintain team rhythms and internal communications that keep the organization aligned.

title: Senior System Software Engineer - Datacenter Power Management
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is redefining accelerated computing and powering the next era of artificial intelligence. Our data-center platforms bring together GPUs, CPUs, networking, systems, and software to solve some of the world’s most exciting computing problems. We are looking for a Senior System Software Engineer to join NVIDIA’s Datacenter Performance and Power Management Software team. You will be responsible for architecting production software for datacenter power management controllers. Your work will also cover cluster- level dynamic provisioning and power-management control system technologies for next-generation data-centers.

You will work at the intersection of hardware architecture, embedded firmware, device drivers, operating systems, and AI workloads. Your responsibilities will span the entire product lifecycle—from initial architectural design and pre-silicon validation through silicon bring-up, productization, and deployment in extensive data-center infrastructures. This is an outstanding chance to influence how next-generation NVIDIA GPUs provide top-tier performance, energy efficiency, and reliability.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Architect, build, implement, and debug data center power and performance-management software, with particular emphasis on end-to-end power management at racks and data halls.
  • Develop real-time controllers, policies, and mechanisms that dynamically optimize performance, power, thermals, and energy efficiency under demanding data-center workloads.
  • Drive features across the full product lifecycle: requirements, architecture, implementation, pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, productization, and production support.
  • Collaborate with GPU architects and hardware designers to define hardware-software interfaces and influence the power-management capabilities of next-generation processors.
  • Analyze complex interactions among workloads, clocks, voltages, power limits, thermals, telemetry, and system-level policies.
  • Lead the investigation and resolution of complex power, performance, stability, and reliability issues spanning firmware, drivers, hardware, and platform software.
  • Develop validation strategies and automation for functional correctness, transition latency, performance-per-watt, and robustness across operating conditions.
  • Build clear architecture, interface, and compose specifications for new power-management features.
  • Partner with geographically distributed architecture, ASIC, firmware, driver, validation, platform, and data-center systems teams.

What We Need to See:

  • BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent experience.
  • At least 12+ years of extensive industry experience crafting system software, embedded firmware, device drivers, or other hardware-related production software.
  • Strong programming skills in C, including experience developing, debugging, and maintaining complex low-level software.
  • Deep understanding of operating-system fundamentals, device-driver architecture, embedded or real-time software, concurrency, interrupt handling, and hardware programming.
  • Experience interpreting hardware specifications and developing software interfaces for registers, telemetry, interrupts, and control mechanisms.
  • Strong understanding of computer architecture and hardware-software interactions.
  • Proven ability to independently debug complex problems across multiple software and hardware layers.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of working effectively across organizational and geographic boundaries.

Ways to Stand Out From the Crowd:

  • Background with architecting, designing, or implementing datacenter provisioning, monitoring, and managing power at a CSP/NCP.
  • Hands-on experience with GPU, CPU, accelerator, or SoC power and performance management.
  • Background with crafting or implementing P-state selection, DVFS, clock-control, voltage-control, power-capping, thermal-management, throttling, or workload-aware control policies.
  • Experience developing real-time feedback controllers, including reasoning about stability, responsiveness, hysteresis, latency, and noisy telemetry.
  • Understanding of electrical and platform considerations such as voltage-frequency relationships, transient power, thermal limits, power delivery, and system-level power budgets.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5; and 272,000 USD – 431,250 USD for Level 6.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Power Validation Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent.


As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA is looking for motivated System Power Validation Engineers to use your creativity to work at NVIDIA with the highly inventive team.


What you'll be doing:

System/board level debug and validation of NVIDIA's products in fields like GPU cards, MGX servers, automotive, robotics, industrial PC, and consumer electronics to ensure the highest quality products reach the market.

  • Managing and accomplishing system power bring-up and debug processes.
  • Collaborating with power vendors to resolve issues and improve our power solutions.
  • Develop and simulate power solution test platforms.
  • Supporting the improvement of future products and power solution roadmaps.
  • Working closely with the design, validation, system design, system validation, silicon design, thermal/mechanical design teams, and vendors to root cause bugs and issues.
  • Contributing to the development of new power validation procedures

What we need to see:

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Power Electronics/Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related degree (or equivalent experience).
  • 2+ years of related experience in power validation.
  • Proven understanding of power electronics fundamentals, with experience in closed-loop control, innovative 48V topologies, multiphase regulators, high power density architecture, Power Distribution Network (PDN) impedance analysis, power devices, and power management.
  • Deep technical knowledge of telemetry and protection management, design for debugging, security, safety and reliability, and failure analysis.
  • Experience with power circuit design, magnetics, modeling, failure analysis, performance analysis, bring-up, debug, and verification.
  • Proficiency in various programming and scripting languages, including C/C++ and JavaScript, as well as Linux.
  • Proficiency with development and simulation tools, lab equipment setup, and fixing skills.
  • Team-oriented demeanor, with a "can do" attitude and excitement for solving multi-disciplinary challenges in fast-paced, layered environments.

descriptionHtml:

We are seeking a Senior Staff Software Engineer to define the technical strategy for autonomous AI-driven enterprise operations at NVIDIA. You will set the architecture that transforms IT from manual, reactive workflows into agentic platforms operating at global scale. This is senior individual contributor role on the team: you will own the hardest technical problems, establish the standards that other engineering organizations adopt, and be accountable for architectural decisions whose consequences compound for years. Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills are vital for success.


What You’ll Be Doing:

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you will define how NVIDIA builds and operates autonomous enterprise systems. Your influence will be measured in systems adopted, engineers elevated, and problems that stopped being problems.

Core responsibilities include:

  • Own the technical strategy and reference architecture for agentic AI across enterprise IT : agent runtimes, tool interfaces, memory and context management, orchestration, evaluation harnesses, and safety guardrails and establish them as the standard that partner engineering organizations build on.
  • Architect and personally build production agentic systems using LLM-based agents, tool calling, RAG, and orchestration frameworks, delivering AI-assisted operations across employee support, endpoint services, and IT support operations.
  • Design autonomous agents that execute complex, multi-step enterprise workflows end-to-end, coordinating approvals, vendor handoffs, cross-system data reconciliation, and exception handling with human-in-the-loop controls and own the reliability, observability, failure semantics, and blast-radius controls that make autonomy safe at enterprise scale.
  • Own the architecture of the integration and automation platform spanning ServiceNow, ERP and procurement systems, and endpoint-management platforms, including infrastructure, data pipelines, APIs, and user-facing applications and make the build/buy/deprecate calls that shape it for the next several years.
  • Define the engineering standards for how agentic systems are built, tested, evaluated, and operated: prompt and tool versioning, offline and online evals, regression suites, cost and latency budgets, security and data-governance patterns, and systematic failure-mode analysis.
  • Drive technical alignment across organizational boundaries, partner engineering teams, platform owners, security, and senior leadership resolving contested architectural decisions and building consensus without formal authority.
  • Multiply the organization. Mentor and grow senior and staff engineers through design partnership, code review, and technical coaching, and raise the engineering bar through the work you ship and the standards you enforce.

What We Need To See:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field, or equivalent experience. 12+ years of hands-on software engineering experience building and operating production systems at scale, with deep expertise in at least one of: Infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, Platform, or Production Engineering.

title: Senior Applied Research Scientist – GPU Native Numerical Algorithms
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA pioneered accelerated computing. Today, we are building software, systems, and research platforms that help scientists and engineers solve problems that were once out of reach. We are looking for an Applied Research Scientist to join our computational engineering applied research team! In this role, we will work together to design GPU-native numerical methods that make engineering simulation faster, more reliable, and easier to use across NVIDIA platforms, while providing the numerical foundations for emerging AI-native engineering algorithms. You will explore solver algorithms, build research prototypes, compare approaches on representative workloads, and help move promising ideas into software used by researchers, engineers, and partners. The goal is not simply to port established CPU algorithms, but to rethink methods around massive parallelism, hierarchical memory, reduced synchronization, mixed precision, tensor-core computation, and multi-GPU systems.

This role connects numerical analysis, accelerated computing, production-minded software engineering, and the co-design of future AI-native engineering methods. We are interested in candidates who enjoy working across math, code, hardware, and real engineering applications. Come help us shape the future of simulation on GPUs!

What you'll be doing:

We work as a team, and you will help us:

  • Invent and reformulate numerical algorithms whose mathematical and computational structure is co-designed for modern NVIDIA GPU architectures, including implicit and explicit engineering simulation.

  • Develop linear and nonlinear solver approaches, including Newton-Krylov methods, multigrid and AMG, domain decomposition, matrix-free algorithms, mixed precision methods, sparse iterative and direct methods, and preconditioning strategies.

  • Investigate when established CPU-oriented numerical methods should be reformulated or replaced for GPU architectures, including new approaches to synchronization-avoiding Krylov methods, GPU-native multigrid and domain decomposition, matrix-free implicit methods, mixed-precision algorithms, and sparse direct/iterative hybrids.

  • Evaluate algorithms on workloads in mechanics, contact, thermal-fluid systems, electromagnetics, semiconductor process and device simulation, EDA, multiphysics, and related CAE domains.

  • Collaborate with CUDA-X, Warp, solver engineering, NVIDIA Research, universities, and industry partners to move useful research from prototype to NVIDIA software capabilities.

  • Help shape the long-term applied research roadmap for GPU-native numerical methods and their evolution toward AI-native computational engineering.

What we need to see:

  • PhD or equivalent experience in computational mechanics, applied mathematics, scientific computing, computer science, aerospace, mechanical, civil engineering, or a related technical field.

  • 5+ years of relevant work/research experience.

  • Research or engineering experience with PDE discretization, finite element, finite volume, discontinuous Galerkin methods, nonlinear solvers, sparse linear algebra, preconditioning, or high-performance computing.

  • Experience writing numerical software in C++ and Python, plus experience developing or optimizing CUDA or GPU code.

descriptionHtml:

descriptionHtml:

Our team works at the intersection of compilers, agentic systems, numerical correctness, and verification to create compiler systems that can reason about, generate, optimize, and validate code transformations across software and hardware boundaries.


In this role, you will help design and build advanced compiler and verification systems that improve developer productivity, system performance, and confidence in correctness. This includes developing compiler-oriented agents and workflows, building numerical validation and verification infrastructure, and co-designing with NVIDIA's compiler, runtime, library, and hardware teams to bring new capabilities into production tools and products.


What you'll be doing:

  • Design, build, and optimize intelligent low-level compiler systems, including compiler-oriented agents, multi-step transformation workflows, tool use, memory, and orchestration.
  • Develop systems that can reason about low-level IR, code generation, optimization passes, scheduling, numerical precision, and performance tradeoffs across GPU-centric workloads.
  • Build the data, environments, verification, reward, and evaluation systems needed to continuously improve compiler quality, numerical correctness, robustness, and performance.
  • Develop infrastructure for numerical validation, differential testing, regression detection, and correctness verification for generated or transformed code.
  • Co-design compiler and verification workflows across NVIDIA's software stack, spanning models and inference, compiler pipelines, runtimes, libraries, kernels, and GPUs.
  • Collaborate closely with internal compiler, CUDA, library, runtime, and hardware teams to integrate new compiler, agentic, and verification capabilities into NVIDIA products.
  • Drive performance analysis and optimization for generated or transformed code, with a strong focus on correctness, scalability, and real-world deployment.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent experience; MS or PhD preferred.
  • 5+ years of relevant industry or academic experience in compilers, AI systems, numerical computing, verification, high-performance computing, or related areas.
  • Strong hands-on experience in compiler implementation, program analysis, code generation, optimization, low-level performance engineering, or correctness infrastructure.
  • Experience in one or more of the following areas: agent systems, coding agents, compiler automation, numerical analysis, program verification, differential testing, or formal/semi-formal validation methods.
  • Strong C/C++ and Python programming skills, with solid software engineering fundamentals; experience with Rust is a plus.
  • Experience with GPU programming and performance optimization using CUDA or comparable accelerator platforms.
  • Ability to work effectively across system boundaries, from model-driven workflows and compiler infrastructure to runtime and hardware-aware optimization.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Track record of building high-impact compiler infrastructure, coding agents, verification frameworks, correctness tooling, or developer tools.
  • Deep expertise in low-level compiler stacks such as LLVM, MLIR, PTX, Triton, or other IR/codegen frameworks.
  • Experience building or optimizing AI-assisted compilation, numerical validation systems, equivalence checking, autotuning, or compiler verification workflows.
  • Deep expertise in GPU systems, numerical behavior, and performance optimization, demonstrated through benchmark results, deployed systems, publications, or widely used software.
  • Publications or open-source leadership in compilers, numerical computing, verification, formal methods, agentic AI, high-performance computing, AI systems, or programming systems.

With highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology industry's most desirable employers. We have some of the most brilliant and hardworking people in the world working with us and our product lines are growing fast in some of the hottest state of the art fields such as Virtual Reality, Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Autonomous Vehicles.

title: DSX Electrical Engineer
descriptionHtml:

Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing.
