Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.


Join NVIDIA, a leader in AI infrastructure, as a DSX Electrical Engineer in Santa Clara, CA! You will work closely with engineers, owners, operators, contractors, and technology partners. Your role is essential in advancing AI infrastructure at large scale. This position lets you use your field experience to develop reference builds, provide technical mentorship, and validate programs for dependable, high-density data center power systems. Your efforts will improve site planning, build, construction, and deployment. This results in clearer builds, quicker technical decisions, and fewer issues.


What you'll be doing:

  • Building strong feedback loops with electrical engineering teams at NVIDIA Cloud Partners, data center providers, EPC firms, facility infrastructure OEMs, system integrators, and AI infrastructure operators.
  • Translating recurring build and deployment friction into clear requirements for DSX product management and engineering roadmaps.
  • Collaborating across NVIDIA, and with partners, to build and publish practical technical assets for DSX electrical deployments, including reference power architectures, design guides, deployment playbooks, equipment selection mentorship, validated examples, and troubleshooting content.
  • Leading technical workshops, architecture reviews, and build deep dives to help partners apply DSX electrical reference builds to new and existing AI factory sites.
  • Supporting early-access and field-validation programs for DSX electrical solutions, testing reference builds and operating assumptions against real sites, high-density AI Compute racks, and dynamic GPU power behavior before broader release.
  • Working across DSX engineering, product management, solution architecture, deployment, and developer marketing to align technical content with product capabilities and deployment needs.
  • Representing the DSX Electrical field at customer forums, technical conferences, industry working sessions, and partner events, presenting credible engineering mentorship and bringing subject area insights back to the product teams.

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in Electrical Engineering, with a Professional Engineer license or equivalent experience.
  • 12 or more years of experience in data center electrical build, construction, commissioning, systems engineering, solutions architecture, technical product management, or a related customer-facing engineering role.
  • Deep knowledge of the electrical power path from utility service through high-, medium-, and low-voltage distribution to mechanical loads and IT racks.
  • Hands-on experience with generators, microgrids, BESS, UPS systems, RPPs, busway, rack power supplies or power shelves, and the electrical interfaces for chillers, cooling towers, CRAC units, and CRAH units.
  • Experience crafting or evaluating electrical systems for high rack power densities, including load behavior, redundancy, protection, maintainability, and operational change.
  • Expertise in short-circuit, selective-coordination, and arc-flash studies, plus a strong understanding of electrical control sequences and Sequence of Operations.
  • Working knowledge of mechanical, controls, life-safety, and IT networking systems that collaborate with data center electrical infrastructure.
  • Ability to turn complex engineering topics into clear written mentorship, technical presentations, training, and productive develop discussions for varied technical audiences.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience applying electrical reference architectures to large-scale GPU clusters, AI factories, or accelerated-computing deployments.
  • Knowledge of dynamic power behavior and mitigation strategies for large GPU deployments.
  • Hands-on expertise with battery energy storage systems, on-site generation, microgrids, microgrid controllers, or utility interconnection requirements.
  • Familiarity with 800 VDC power distribution, international electrical systems, and the adaptation of global standards to regional codes and construction practices.
  • A record of crafting technical communities, industry mentorship, reference builds, training programs, or standards that engineering teams actively use. Demonstrated ability to convey complex technical topics to engineers as well as strategic direction to executives.

descriptionHtml:

We're united in our quest to transform the way graphics are used to solve some of the most complex problems in computer science.

The GPU started out as an engine for simulating human imagination, conjuring up the amazing virtual worlds of video games and Hollywood films. Today, NVIDIA’s GPU simulates human intelligence, running deep learning algorithms and acting as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. NVIDIA is increasingly known as “the AI computing company.”

What you’ll be doing:

  • Build reusable bus functional models, monitors, checkers and scoreboards following coverage driven verification methodology.

  • Expected to understand the design specification and implementation, define the verification scope, develop test plans, tests, and the verification infrastructure and verify the correctness of the design.

  • You will be collaborating with architects, designers, and pre and post silicon verification teams to accomplish your tasks.

What we need to see:

  • 1+ years of relevant experience

  • Experience in verification at Unit/Sub-system/SOC level and expertise in Verilog and SystemVerilog

  • Expertise in comprehensive verification of IP or interconnect protocols (e.g. PCI Express, USB, SATA)

  • Experience in developing and working in functional coverage based constrained random verification environments

  • Background in DV methodologies like UVM/VMM and exposure to industry standard verification tools for simulation and debug

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Excellent knowledge of PCIE protocol - Gen3 and above

  • Good understanding of the system level architecture of PCIE/CXL-based designs

  • Perl, Python or similar scripting and SW programming language experience

  • Good debugging and analytical skills

  • Good interpersonal skills & dream to work as a great teammate

title: Senior Compiler Engineer - AI
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI — the next era of computing — with the GPU acting as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. Today, we are increasingly known as "the AI computing company".


NVIDIA is hiring world class Software Engineers with AI Compiler and distributed systems experience for its Deep Learning Compiler Technology team. The team builds JaxPP, NVIDIA's open-source library for pipeline parallelism in JAX. JaxPP turns a JAX training program into per-stage tasks and runs them across many GPUs. With it, very large models can be trained on NVIDIA GPU clusters using unmodified JAX and XLA. Join the team that is developing advanced compiler and runtime technology for the entire deep learning community.


What you'll be doing:

  • Design and implement program transformations on JAX programs (jaxpr) for large-scale training, on top of unmodified JAX and XLA: pipeline schedules, placement of tasks across stages, sharding (including JAX explicit sharding), and overlap of communication with computation.
  • Develop technologies and products involving optimizing compilers and runtime execution frameworks for accelerating deep learning training on large scale distributed systems.
  • Work on compiling a graph intermediate representation (IR) to target specific code, and build the distributed runtime that dispatches per-stage programs to many GPUs and moves data between stages through communication libraries such as NCCL.
  • Contribute to advancing the state of the art in compiler technology for delivering high performance on large-scale training workloads, including mixture-of-experts models.
  • Collaborate with members of the software framework teams (for example JAX and XLA) and the hardware architecture teams to accelerate the next generation of deep learning software, and work on integrating JaxPP into JAX training frameworks, including MaxText.
  • Be a core contributor to the open-source JaxPP project: keeping it working with new JAX releases, testing, performance tracking, and working with teams who adopt it for their training runs.

What we need to see:

  • Masters or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field or equivalent experience.
  • 6+ years of relevant work or research experience in compilers, distributed systems, or deep learning training.
  • Compiler design and implementation.
  • Distributed system design, development, and deployment.
  • Experience with deep learning frameworks (JAX, PyTorch).
  • GPU training and inference of deep learning models.
  • C/C++ and Python programming, with excellent software design skills, including debugging, performance analysis, and test design.
  • Experience with parallel computing libraries (MPI).
  • Be able to work independently, define project goals and scope, and lead your own development efforts.
  • Strong communication skills are required, including working directly with engineers at partner companies to debug and tune large training runs, along with the ability to work in a dynamic product-oriented team.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience with JAX internals (jaxpr, tracing, sharding, shard_map), or with XLA, StableHLO, or MLIR.
  • Experience building or tuning large training jobs with pipeline, tensor, expert, and data parallelism, for example in MaxText or Megatron-LM, and debugging their performance on large GPU clusters.
  • Knowledge of GPU communication libraries such as NCCL, NVSHMEM, or RDMA, and of CPU and/or GPU architecture. CUDA programming experience is a plus.
  • Contributions to open-source compiler or machine learning projects.
  • Experience in mentoring early career engineers and interns is a bonus.

title: Senior Research Scientist - Autonomous Vehicles
descriptionHtml:
We are now seeking a Sr Research Scientist for Autonomous Vehicles! NVIDIA is recruiting top Senior Research Scientists for Autonomous Vehicle Research! AI-powered autonomous vehicles that can learn, reason, and interact with people are no longer science fiction. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery vehicles, and autonomous construction vehicles, among others, are getting increasingly close to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research questions still need to be addressed for us to achieve full vehicle autonomy. For instance, how can we: Enable novel training paradigms that leverage simulation to train AV policies in closed-loop? Equip autonomous vehicles with online and offline assurances that meet the standards for safety-critical systems? Ensure that autonomous vehicles work seamlessly in new places?


These are some of the exciting questions that the NVIDIA Autonomous Vehicle Research group is tackling. We bring together a diverse, interdisciplinary research team working on core topics in vehicle autonomy, including agent behavior models, end-to-end AV architectures, AI safety, closed-loop training approaches, and AV foundation models (VLMs, reasoning models, etc.). Our focus is on basic and applied research; lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source code as well as provide real-world impact by deploying technology within production systems. NVIDIA is well known for its team culture, and lab researchers are able to closely interact with others within the company who are experts in perception systems, machine learning, and robotics. There is an opportunity to make a strong impact on products, while having the freedom and bandwidth to conduct ground-breaking publishable research.


What you'll be doing:

  • Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques in the field of vehicle autonomy.
  • Publish and present your original research, speak at conferences and events.
  • Collaborate with other research team members, a diverse set of internal product teams, and external researchers.
  • Have a broader impact through the transfer and/or open-source of the technology you've developed to relevant product groups.
  • Collaborate closely with product teams to transfer research results into high-end, production-level systems.

What we need to see:

  • Ph.D. in Computer Science/Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 6+ years of relevant research experience in the field of vehicle / robot autonomy.
  • Strong knowledge of theory and practice of vehicle / robot autonomy, or a related area with a strong interest in connecting your work to autonomous vehicles.
  • A track record of research excellence with your work published in top conferences and journals such as RSS, ICRA, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc, and other research artifacts such as software projects
  • Excellent collaboration and interpersonal skills
  • Exceptional programming skills in Python; C++ and parallel programming (e.g., CUDA).
  • Solid understanding of common machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch and Tensorflow.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required along with the ability to work in a dynamic, research-focused team.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. Are you a creative and autonomous research scientist with a genuine passion for advancing the state of AI? If so, we want to hear from you!

title: BlueField Platform Technical Lead
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a BlueField Platform Tech Lead — a senior individual contributor who will own the end-to-end technical architecture of the BF platform stack. This role is the single authoritative voice across both the ARM SoC / boot firmware layer (ATF, UEFI, Linux bring-up) and the BMC layer (Yocto, embedded Linux, platform management). You will guide current BlueField generations and set the technical direction for future ones. Do you enjoy leading the whole system rather than one piece of it, and making the decisions that keep it working together? This position is for you.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Own the end-to-end technical architecture and roadmap for the
  • BlueField platform. This covers SoC boot, platform firmware (ATF/UEFI), the DPU BMC, and the interfaces between the DPU, the host and the BMC.
  • Set the platform’s technical direction with architecture, hardware, NIC firmware, software stack and product teams. Make sure decisions stay consistent across BlueField generations and product variants.
  • Define and maintain platform interface contracts, including boot and reset flows, firmware update and recovery, platform management (Redfish, PLDM, MCTP, IPMI), and BMC–SoC communication.
  • Own platform security architecture together with the security teams: secure boot, measured boot, attestation, key and provisioning flows, and secure firmware update.
  • Act as the technical lead for new silicon and board bring-up. Assess hardware issues, define workarounds, and drive readiness criteria for achievements and releases.
  • Serve as the technical reference for customers and partners. Translate platform requirements and use cases into architecture and design decisions.
  • Assess emerging technologies, standards, tools and development methods, such as automation, emulation/simulation, observability and failure triage. Drive adoption where they improve product quality, engineering efficiency or time to debug.
  • Raise the organization’s technical skills through build reviews, technical mentorship and collaborative discussions.

What we need to see:

  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field.
  • 12+ years of experience in embedded, firmware or Linux system software.
  • Deep expertise in at least one of the two domains below, and solid working knowledge of the other:
  • ARM platform boot: ATF, UEFI/EDK II, bootloaders, Linux kernel bring-up, device tree/ACPI, platform initialization
  • BMC and platform management: OpenBMC, Redfish interface, PLDM protocol, MCTP communication, IPMI standards, firmware update flows
  • A strong grasp of platform security principles, including secure boot, chain of trust and firmware security.
  • A record of leading difficult cross-organizational technical projects from definition through delivery, including decisions with material product or schedule impact.
  • Experience influencing architecture and product direction through technical judgment, without relying on direct management authority.
  • Strong C skills and practical experience in Linux development, debugging, and hardware/software integration.
  • Excellent communication and technical presentation skills, including with customers and senior stakeholders.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Hands-on experience with both ARM SoC/server boot flows (ATF, UEFI) and BMC software (OpenBMC, Yocto).
  • Experience with trusted boot processes, attestation (SPDM), provisioning, firmware update or recovery architectures.
  • Knowledge of server-platform interfaces: PCIe, I2C/I3C, SPI, SMBus, NC-SI, and reset and power sequencing.
  • Experience with DPU, SmartNIC or data-center server platforms, and with networking protocols.
  • Experience building automated test, emulation, observability or failure-triage infrastructure, or introducing tools that clearly improved team efficiency.

title: Lead User Experience Researcher - IT and Employee Productivity
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. Today, we're tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. NVIDIA IT builds the products NVIDIANs use to get work done every day: the company intranet and mobile app, IT help and self-service, an AI personal assistant, and secure workspaces where employees run their own AI agents. We're hiring our first user experience researcher to answer a question that matters more every quarter: what makes people productive at NVIDIA, and what should we build, buy, or change so more people can work that way?


This is a senior, independent role with a long horizon. Our users are our colleagues, so access is never the bottleneck. You start with rich data: an annual IT survey with thousands of written comments from employees in 36 countries, support tickets, and product analytics. You'll set the research agenda, run the studies that matter most, and raise the research bar for the product managers and designers you work with.


What you'll be doing:

  • Own a multi-quarter research program on how NVIDIANs work: what separates people who have adopted new ways of working, including AI tools, from those who haven't, and which tools, built or bought, would help the rest.
  • Shape our core products. Find the fundamental changes that would make our intranet, IT help, and AI assistant more useful, starting from questions like "what does a typical work day at NVIDIA look like?"
  • Pair field research (contextual inquiry, interviews, diary studies) with survey, support, and analytics data. Use AI to scale analysis without trading away validity.
  • Bring rigor. Choose methods that hold up (reliability, validity, sampling), and help the team distinguish between decisions that benefit from research vs. decisions that can just be made.
  • Raise the team's research craft. Coach PMs and designers on study design, interview guides, and live interviewing, and partner with designers on usability work
  • Build the practice from zero: a participant panel, consent and confidentiality standards for research with colleagues (with HR and Legal), and an insights repository so research compounds instead of repeating.
  • Turn findings into decisions. Present clear recommendations to IT leadership, define experience and adoption metrics with PMs, and follow through until insights shape roadmaps, not just fixes.

What we need to see:

  • 12+ years in UX research or a closely related field, including leading strategic, multi-quarter research programs.
  • Master's or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Anthropology, Sociology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Deep mixed-methods expertise: generative field research, survey design and analysis (including open text), and analysis of behavioral data.
  • A portfolio or case studies showing research that changed strategy, roadmap, or investment decisions, not only feature details.
  • Experience researching enterprise, internal, or workplace products used by employees.
  • Proven ability to work as the first or only researcher on a team: set the agenda, say no to low-value studies, and coach others on research craft.
  • Clear writing and presentation that moves senior leaders to a decision.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Research on AI tool adoption, knowledge-worker productivity, or how teams change the way they work.
  • Internal IT, employee experience, or workplace technology research.
  • Quantitative depth: SQL, R, or Python, and quasi-experimental designs (such as matched comparisons) that separate what drives adoption from what only correlates with it.
  • You've used LLMs to scale research synthesis and know where they fail.

title: Senior Systems Software Engineer - HPC and AI Storage
descriptionHtml:

You will lead technical analyses, transform workload insights into engineering fixes, and guide the formulation and implementation of storage policies. You will handle storage integration, testing, and rollout while coordinating with engineering groups on hardware and software projects. This role supports the efficiency and dependability encouraged at datacenter scale.


What you'll be doing:

  • Engineer and integrate storage systems for large-scale HPC and AI clusters, including Lustre, NFS, and their interaction with compute nodes, networks, and storage hardware.
  • Examine performance and reliability issues throughout the I/O stack, supervising application behavior across filesystem clients, Linux kernel paths, network protocols, servers, and storage devices.
  • Develop software fixes and performance improvements, working with NVIDIA engineering teams, storage partners, and open-source maintainers to bring changes through review, testing, and deployment.
  • Characterize real application I/O, including training-data access, checkpoint and restart, metadata-intensive operations, and concurrent workloads. Translate findings into improvements to software, and system configuration and design.
  • Build reproducible benchmarks, diagnostic tools, and regression tests that measure efficiency, latency, metadata performance, scalability, and behavior under contention.
  • Lead storage qualification and commissioning, validating functionality, data integrity, failure recovery, and sustained performance at cluster scale.
  • Define and implement storage placement, caching, and data lifecycle policies informed by workload requirements, capacity, and operational evidence.

What we need to see:

  • Deep engineering experience with Lustre, NFS, or comparable shared storage systems, including implementation-level debugging in at least one stack and experience integrating storage into Linux clusters.
  • Strong C programming and Linux debugging skills, with experience reading, modifying, and diagnosing kernel or user-space storage software.
  • Understanding of filesystem and distributed-system behavior, including metadata operations, caching and consistency, locking, concurrency, client/server communication, and recovery.
  • Experience analyzing application access patterns and tuning filesystem or storage-stack behavior to deliver performance improvements.
  • Ability to take a complex performance or correctness problem from initial symptoms through reproduction, root-cause analysis, implementation, and validation.
  • Proficiency in Python and shell scripting to build maintainable diagnostic, test automation, and analysis tools.
  • Ability to independently lead technical efforts, influence design decisions across teams, and communicate findings and tradeoffs clearly.
  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or equivalent practical experience, with 12+ years of relevant experience.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Expertise in Lustre metadata and client I/O, Linux VFS and page cache, NFS protocol and client/server internals, or distributed locking and recovery.
  • Experience with hierarchical storage management, policy engines, or migration between filesystems and object storage, including data recall and recovery from interrupted transfers.
  • Experience with RDMA storage transports, GPUDirect Storage, or optimizing data loading and checkpointing for GPU workloads.
  • Experience with storage security and multi-tenancy, including authentication, identity mapping, permissions, and encryption.

title: Principal Software Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to drive the architecture and development of our bare-metal and cloud compute infrastructure. Our organization supports hundreds of megawatts of datacenter capacity, making a growing physical fleet available as reliable, secure, and efficient compute services for NVIDIA engineering.


We operate an NVIDIA GPU Private cloud that provides infrastructure for continuous integration and validation. Hardware, firmware, drivers, networking, and system software are coordinated and tested on their path to production. The fleet includes x86 and Arm servers, GPUs, DPUs, high-speed networking, storage, and rack-scale systems. Platforms include Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin. In this senior individual contributor role, you will combine hands-on software engineering with architectural leadership. You will evolve our OpenStack platform, automate infrastructure operations, and address complex systems challenges across multiple datacenters.


What you'll be doing:

  • Own architecture and lead implementation of large-scale OpenStack infrastructure supporting bare-metal provisioning, virtual machines, and engineering workloads spanning several datacenters around the globe.
  • Architect and implement Infrastructure as Code frameworks to automate provisioning, configuration, and lifecycle management across OpenStack and bare-metal environments, using version-controlled definitions, automated validation, drift detection, and safe rollback.
  • Build and improve compute control planes, resource scheduling, topology-aware placement, reservations, and capacity management for heterogeneous hardware.
  • Develop and extend OpenStack services and integrations, including Nova, Neutron, Ironic, Cinder, Keystone, and Placement, based on platform requirements.
  • Improve platform scalability, availability, and performance through architectural changes, profiling, failure analysis, and detailed elimination of operational bottlenecks.
  • Build safe deployment, upgrade, migration, and rollback mechanisms that minimize disruption to engineering workloads.
  • Partner with SRE, datacenter operations, security, product engineering teams to onboard new platforms and resolve failures across system boundaries.

What we need to see:

  • 15+ years of proven experience in software engineering, distributed systems, or cloud infrastructure, demonstrating leadership in diverse technical initiatives across teams. BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Deep experience crafting, developing, deploying, and fixing production OpenStack environments, particularly Nova, Neutron, and Ironic.
  • Strong software development skills in Python and experience building maintainable services, APIs, and infrastructure automation.
  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, including concurrency, state management, asynchronous workflows, failure handling, and recovery.
  • Deep Linux systems knowledge and experience with virtualization, KVM/QEMU, containers, and guest operating-system provisioning.
  • Proven understanding of cloud networking, including L2/L3 networking, VLANs, overlays, DHCP, PXE boot, routing, and tenant isolation.
  • Experience with databases and messaging infrastructure supporting cloud control planes, such as MySQL/MariaDB and RabbitMQ.
  • Experience operating infrastructure with demanding reliability requirements, including monitoring, incident response, system resources, and production upgrades.
  • Excellent debugging skills across hardware, firmware, operating systems, communication systems, data storage, and distributed services.
  • Ability to translate ambiguous requirements into technical direction and influence engineering teams across organizational boundaries and time zones.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Contributions to OpenStack or related open-source projects, including upstream features, bug fixes, performance improvements, or architectural proposals.
  • Experience scaling OpenStack across multiple regions or datacenters, including control-plane resilience, fleet upgrades, and workload migration.
  • Expertise in Ironic, Redfish, BMC integration, and provisioning or recovering large bare-metal fleets. Experience with Ceph, distributed storage, and storage integration with OpenStack.
  • Experience with GPU and Arm platforms, PCIe pass-through, SR-IOV, NVLink, InfiniBand, or high-speed Ethernet.
  • A record of delivering architectural improvements that measurably increase reliability, scalability, utilization, or developer efficiency.

title: Senior Engineering Manager, Object Storage - DGX Cloud
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA's Object Storage Platform team builds and operates the company's internal S3-compatible distributed object storage service — a critical piece of infrastructure that stores, manages, and serves exabytes of data across NVIDIA's on-premises and hybrid environments. This platform is the storage backbone for NVIDIA's AI infrastructure, enabling researchers and engineers to reliably store massive datasets, model checkpoints, and training artifacts at scale. We are seeking a seasoned Engineering Manager to lead the Object Storage platform team with both dev and SRE responsibilities. You will own the full software development and service delivery lifecycle — from roadmap planning through production operations — while building a high-performance engineering culture grounded in technical excellence, service reliability, and continuous delivery.


What You'll Be Doing:

  • Own roadmap execution for NVIDIA's internal object storage service — partnering with internal customers, Product Management, and Architecture to translate multi-quarter goals into clear engineering plans with measurable milestones.

Represent the Object Storage engineering organization to senior leadership, providing transparent status updates, surfacing risks early, and advocating for the resources needed to succeed.

Experience managing capacity planning, cost optimization, and chargeback modeling for shared internal storage infrastructure.

title: AI Infrastructure and Frameworks Intern, Cosmos Lab - 2027
descriptionHtml:
Join NVIDIA’s Cosmos Lab Infrastructure team to develop training and post-training systems for advanced Physical AI models, including world foundation models and robot policies. Our infrastructure connects training, inference, and evaluation with simulation and real-world robot interaction. You will work with a mentor on a focused project scoped to your experience and internship duration, implementing and evaluating systems improvements on real AI workloads using NVIDIA’s GPU infrastructure.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Develop and optimize training infrastructure for advanced Physical AI world models, supporting pre-training, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL). Explore distributed parallelism, sharding, low-precision training, compute–communication overlap, and numerical consistency and efficient weight synchronization between training and inference.
  • Build Physical AI post-training and RL infrastructure supporting advanced training algorithms. Connect simulation or, where applicable, real-robot interaction with experience collection, rollout inference, reward computation, training, and evaluation. Optimize these workflows through partitioning, pipelining, data transfer, and synchronization across synchronous, asynchronous, or disaggregated execution.
  • Improve efficiency and scalability across training, inference, simulation, and evaluation through scheduling, placement, dynamic resource allocation, and load balancing, supporting heterogeneous resources, elasticity, and fault recovery.
  • Analyze and optimize system performance, working with researchers to investigate, support, and compare emerging Physical AI models, training workflows, and algorithms from a systems perspective. Use profiling, benchmarking, and performance modeling to identify bottlenecks and measure throughput, latency, GPU utilization, and policy freshness. Share findings through tested code, documentation, and technical presentations, and contribute to research publications where appropriate.

What we need to see:

  • Pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
  • Strong Python and debugging skills, with systems fundamentals in concurrency, distributed execution, memory management, or data movement.
  • Practical experience in at least one area: training infrastructure, RL infrastructure, simulation or robotics integration, or inference infrastructure. Coursework, research, open-source projects, and internships all count.
  • Strong analytical and communication skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn.
  • Experience in every listed area, prior access to large GPU clusters, and model architecture or learning algorithm research are not required.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience optimizing training infrastructure, including distributed parallelism, low-precision training, GPU memory efficiency, or compute–communication overlap.
  • Experience optimizing scheduling, placement, resource allocation, or data transfer across training, rollout, simulation, and evaluation.
  • Experience extending RL pipelines, integrating simulation environments or robot interfaces, or optimizing inference; GPU profiling, C++/CUDA development, and open-source contributions or research in ML systems are also valued.

title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Compute Scheduling
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA is a pioneer in accelerated computing, known for inventing the GPU and driving breakthroughs in gaming, computer graphics, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence. Our technology powers everything from generative AI to autonomous systems, and we continue to shape the future of computing through innovation and collaboration. Within this mission, our team, Managed AI Research Superclusters (MARS), builds and scales the infrastructure, platforms, and tools that enable researchers and engineers to develop the next generation of AI/ML systems. By joining us, you'll help design solutions that power some of the world's most advanced computing workloads.


The MARS Scheduling team decides how NVIDIA's AI research compute gets used. That fleet spans many of the largest GPU clusters in the world, across multiple clouds and partners, running everything from frontier-model pretraining to reinforcement learning and agentic workloads. We run Slurm and Kubernetes at large scale. Our scheduling is coordinated and topology-sensitive on rack-scale systems. We manage fair sharing and quotas for hundreds of research teams. We support preemption and reservations. Elastic jobs recover from failure without losing progress. You will own real parts of the scheduling stack, and the opportunity to ship code into our open-source and internal platform code, and see the result in GPU-hours returned to researchers within days. The researchers training NVIDIA's own models are your users, and they will tell you quickly what works.

What you'll be doing:

  • Design and build scheduling for large GPU fleets on both Slurm and Kubernetes. That covers queueing, gang and topology-aware placement on rack-scale NVLink systems, preemption, reservations and backfill that reaches the end of very deep queues.
  • Build the policy layer: fair share, quotas and allocations across many research teams, driven from a central allocation system and enforced the same way on every scheduler.
  • Run Slurm as a cloud-native service on Kubernetes, and extend Kubernetes batch scheduling (Kueue and its ecosystem) for training, reinforcement learning, sandboxes and inference.
  • Build services around the scheduler: reservation automation, node-health-aware placement, workflow orchestration across clusters, and APIs that let other platforms submit and track work.
  • Measure and raise goodput: GPU occupancy, waste, fairness and time to start for large jobs. Use the data to choose what to build next.
  • Own reliability for the components you build: on-call, incident analysis and fixes that remove whole classes of failure, so problems are found before researchers hit them.
  • Work upstream and across teams: contribute to Slurm, Kubernetes and related open-source projects, and partner with platform, storage, networking and research teams.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 6+ years building production systems software.
  • Deep experience with at least one batch or cluster scheduler, such as Slurm, Kueue, Volcano, KAI, YuniKorn or a scheduler you built. You should be able to explain its internals, not only its configuration.
  • Strong programming in Go, C or C++, plus Python for tooling and analysis.
  • Hands-on Kubernetes experience: controllers or operators, CRDs, scheduling and resource management.
  • Solid Linux systems knowledge: containers (Docker, Podman, Enroot or Apptainer), cgroups, networking basics and debugging under load.
  • A track record of owning a service in production and making it measurably better.
  • Clear written and spoken communication with engineers and researchers.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Experience scheduling large-scale AI training: thousands of GPUs, NVLink and InfiniBand or RoCE topology, multi-node jobs that must start together.
  • Contributions to Slurm, Kubernetes SIG Scheduling, Kueue, Volcano, KAI or similar open-source schedulers.
  • Experience running Slurm on Kubernetes (Slinky or similar), or building Kubernetes operators for batch or HPC workloads.
  • Familiarity with RL, agentic or inference workloads and what they need from a scheduler: heterogeneous jobs, sandboxes, elastic scale and fast restarts.
  • Experience with workflow orchestrators such as Flyte, Airflow, Ray or Kubeflow at scale.
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4; and 224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

title: Senior Signal and Power Integrity Engineer
descriptionHtml:
NVIDIA has continuously reinvented itself over two decades. Our invention of the GPU in 1999 sparked the growth of the PC gaming market, redefined modern computer graphics, and revolutionized parallel computing. More recently, GPU deep learning ignited modern AI - the next era of computing. NVIDIA is a “learning machine” that constantly evolves by adapting to new opportunities that are hard to solve, that only we can tackle, and that matter to the world. This is our life’s work, to amplify human creativity and intelligence!

We are looking for a Senior Signal & Power Integrity Engineer. We work closely with NVIDIA sites in USA and China and have access to extensive knowledge, technologies and tools. Yet we are responsible for our own product line of PHY IC’s . Taking the products from concepting, through design, implementation, verification and release to customers. If you thrive working with highly skilled people that enjoy reaching challenging goals then NVIDIA in might be the perfect workplace for you. This is a dynamic team working with state of the art, unique technology. If you are someone that loves a challenge, come join this diverse team and help move the needle !


What you'll be doing:


  • Design high frequencies channels up to 400Gb/s per lane for PCBs, packages, connectors and cables.
  • Design layout guidelines for our systems.
  • Simulate passive and active elements in 3D and 2D simulation tools
  • Measure systems in the lab using Network Analyzer, TDR and scope
  • Master InfiniBand, Ethernet and PCI-Ex Layer 1 specifications and implementation methods
  • Work in an intense environment and control multi-discipline expertise

What we need to see:


  • B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering (or equivalent experience)
  • 5+ years of experience
  • Familiar with electromagnetics, specifically electromagnetic waves including transmission line theory and via properties.
  • Expert level proficiency with EM tools (such as Ansys EM, CST, etc.).
  • Familiarity with high-speed I/O design concepts including clock generation, transmitter & receiver design, and equalization schemes.
  • Experience in Lab measurements including VNA & TDR experience, interface timing budgets, and system modeling.
  • Master InfiniBand, Ethernet, and PCI-Ex Layer 1 specifications and implementation methods.
  • Ability to work in an intense environment and control multi-discipline expertise.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:


  • M.Sc./Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering and PDN analyses including model generation and time domain simulation.
  • Familiar with NRZ/PAM-4 signaling schemes.
  • Analyses involving co-simulation of circuits and PDN models.
  • Experience with MATLAB, Python, and C.
  • Exposure to TSV (Through-Silicon-Via) modeling and analysis.
